target: Приготовленная мамой еда оказалась очень вкусной.
english: The food prepared by mom turned out to be very delicious.
tip: A passive participle names its agent in the instrumental: приготовленная мамой (prigotovlennaya mamoy = prepared by mom).

target: Она попросила, чтобы мы подождали.
english: She asked us to wait.
tip: A request uses чтобы plus a past-tense verb: чтобы мы подождали (chtoby my podozhdali = for us to wait), not an imperative.

target: Она спросила, когда мы приедем.
english: She asked when we would arrive.
tip: Indirect questions keep the original tense: приедем (priedem = will arrive) stays future, where English uses 'would arrive'.

target: Она спросила, можно ли войти.
english: She asked if she could come in.
tip: For a yes/no indirect question, put ли (li = whether) after the key word: можно ли войти (mozhno li voyti = whether one may enter).

target: Не зная дороги, мы заблудились.
english: Not knowing the way, we got lost.
tip: Не зная (ne znaya = not knowing) is an adverbial participle; it marks action going on at the same time as the main verb.

target: Позавтракав, дети пошли в школу.
english: Having had breakfast, the children went to school.
tip: The -в ending on Позавтракав (pozavtrakav = having had breakfast) marks an action completed before the main verb пошли (poshli = went).

target: Мечтая о путешествиях, он копил деньги.
english: Dreaming about travel, he saved money.
tip: This verb takes о plus prepositional: мечтая о путешествиях (mechtaya o puteshestviyakh = dreaming about travels).

target: Будучи врачом, она знала, что делать.
english: Being a doctor, she knew what to do.
tip: A predicate noun after быть (byt = to be) takes the instrumental: будучи врачом (buduchi vrachom = being a doctor).

target: Проснувшись рано, он пошёл на пробежку.
english: Having woken up early, he went for a run.
tip: Reflexive verbs form the adverbial participle in -вшись: проснувшись (prosnuvshis = having woken up), from проснуться (prosnutsya = to wake up).

target: Она сообщила, что уезжает.
english: She informed that she is leaving.
tip: Russian keeps the spoken tense: уезжает (uezzhaet = is leaving) stays present, where English shifts to 'was leaving'.

target: Считается, что русский язык сложный.
english: Russian is considered difficult.
tip: The -ся verb Считается (schitaetsya = it is considered) is an impersonal passive: no subject, action stated generally.

target: Экзамен был перенесён на следующую пятницу.
english: The exam was postponed to next Friday.
tip: Past passive uses был plus a short participle: был перенесён (byl perenesyon = was postponed).

target: Сколько вам лет, если не секрет?
english: How old are you, if it's not a secret?
tip: Age uses the dative: сколько вам лет (skolko vam let = how old are you), literally 'how many years to you'.

target: Деревья были посажены школьниками в честь праздника.
english: Trees were planted by schoolchildren in honor of the holiday.
tip: In a passive, the agent takes the instrumental: посажены школьниками (posazheny shkolnikami = planted by schoolchildren).

target: Новый дом построен из кирпича и дерева на холме.
english: The new house was built from brick and wood on the hill.
tip: Material uses из plus genitive: построен из кирпича (postroen iz kirpicha = built out of brick).

target: У меня есть один старший брат, который живёт в Москве и работает инженером.
english: I have one older brother who lives in Moscow and works as an engineer.
tip: который (kotoryy = who) takes gender from брат (brat = brother) but its case from its own clause; as subject here it stays nominative.

target: По его словам, всё прошло хорошо.
english: According to his words, everything went well.
tip: по plus dative means 'according to': по его словам (po ego slovam = according to him).

target: Опавшие листья шуршат.
english: The fallen leaves rustle.
tip: Опавшие (opavshie = fallen) is a past participle used like an adjective, agreeing with листья (listya = leaves) in the plural.

target: Река высохла, и смотреть на неё грустно.
english: The river dried up, and it's sad to look at it.
tip: грустно (grustno = sad) with the infinitive смотреть (smotret = to look) means it is sad to look, and needs no subject.

target: Умывшись, он сел завтракать.
english: Having washed up, he sat down to have breakfast.
tip: Умывшись (umyvshis = having washed) is a verbal adverb; the -вшись (-vshis) ending marks a completed action done before he sat down.

target: Выученный урок запомнится надолго.
english: The learned lesson will be remembered for a long time.
tip: Выученный (vyuchenny = learned) is a past passive participle used as an adjective, agreeing with урок (urok = lesson).

target: Будучи студентом, он много читал.
english: Being a student, he read a lot.
tip: Будучи (buduchi = being) is the verbal adverb of быть (byt = to be), and the noun after it goes to instrumental: студентом (studentom = student).

target: Решение было принято после долгого обсуждения.
english: The decision was made after a long discussion.
tip: было принято (bylo prinyato = was made) is a past passive; было agrees with the neuter Решение (reshenie = decision).

target: Я учу русский язык уже полгода.
english: I've been learning Russian for half a year already.
tip: Russian uses the present учу (uchu = I study) with уже полгода (uzhe polgoda = already half a year) where English says I have been studying.

target: Гуляя в парке, мы встретили друга.
english: While walking in the park, we met a friend.
tip: Гуляя (gulyaya = walking) is an imperfective verbal adverb with -я (-ya), showing action at the same time as встретили (vstretili = met).

target: Идущий по улице человек – мой сосед.
english: The person walking along the street is my neighbor.
tip: Идущий (idushchy = walking) is a present active participle, a one-word way to say the man who is walking, agreeing with человек (chelovek = man).

target: Потеряв надежду, он всё равно не сдавался.
english: Having lost hope, he still did not give up.
tip: Потеряв (poteryav = having lost) is a perfective verbal adverb; the -в (-v) ending marks an action finished before he kept going.

target: Новая дорога строится уже третий месяц подряд.
english: The new road has been under construction for three months straight.
tip: строится (stroitsya = is being built) adds -ся (-sya) to make the verb passive: the road is being built, with no builder named.

target: Земля была продана новому владельцу в прошлом году.
english: The land was sold to a new owner last year.
tip: The person sold to takes the dative: новому владельцу (novomu vladeltsu = to the new owner) after была продана (byla prodana = was sold).

target: Замёрзшее озеро блестит.
english: The frozen lake glistens.
tip: Замёрзшее (zamyorzsheye = frozen) is a past participle used like an adjective, agreeing with the neuter озеро (ozero = lake).
